title: Bai with Sa-um (Fermented Pork Fat)
jainNotes: Contains fermented pork fat (sa-um) - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Seasonal vegetables (pumpkin leaves, beans, spinach, etc.)
Bamboo shoot, sa-um (fermented pork fat), chilli, salt

recipe: Boil seasonal vegetables and bamboo shoot with a little sa-um and salt.
Add local herbs and chilli towards the end. Simmer into a light, flavourful stew.
Serve with steamed rice – the quintessential Mizo everyday dish.
tips: Classic Bai with fermented pork fat – the most traditional version.
Sa-um gives the distinctive deep, savoury flavour.

title: Bai with Bekang (Vegetarian)
jainNotes: Contains fermented soybean (bekang). No onion or garlic. Verify fermentation process for Jain compliance.

ingredients.name: Seasonal vegetables (pumpkin leaves, beans, spinach, etc.)
Bamboo shoot, bekang (fermented soybean), chilli, salt

recipe: Boil seasonal vegetables and bamboo shoot with bekang and salt.
Add local herbs and chilli towards the end. Simmer into a light, flavourful stew.
Serve with steamed rice – a vegetarian version of the quintessential Mizo dish.
tips: Vegetarian version of Bai using fermented soybean.
Bekang gives a unique fermented depth without meat.

title: Sawhchiar
jainNotes: Contains meat (chicken or pork), onion, garlic - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Onion, ginger, garlic, local herbs, salt

recipe: Cook rice and meat together with onion, ginger, garlic and herbs, adding enough water for a soft, porridge-like consistency.
Simmer until the rice breaks down and the flavours meld.
Serve hot – a comforting rice-and-meat porridge.
tips: Mizo-style congee – warming and filling.
Anthur (roselle) leaves can be added for a tangy note.

title: Chhum Han
jainNotes: Ingredients are Jain-compatible (mixed vegetables, ginger, green chilli, salt). No onion, garlic, or root vegetables. Verify specific vegetable types.
recipe: Steam or boil the vegetables with ginger and a little chilli until just tender.
Season lightly with salt. Serve as a clean, simple side with rice.
tips: Oil-free steamed vegetables – highlights natural flavours.
A light and healthy accompaniment.

title: Vawksa Rep
jainNotes: Contains smoked pork - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Bamboo shoot, green chilli, local herbs

recipe: Cook the smoked pork until tender. Add bamboo shoot, chilli and herbs.
Simmer so the smoky meat and tangy bamboo shoot flavours combine.
Serve with rice – one of the most loved Mizo dishes.
tips: Smoking the pork over wood is traditional and essential for authentic taste.
Bamboo shoot cuts the richness.

title: Vegetable Bai
jainNotes: Contains onion and garlic - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion-garlic.

ingredients.name: Bekang (fermented soybean), onion, garlic, local herbs, chilli, salt

recipe: Boil the vegetables with bekang, onion, garlic, chilli and salt into a light stew.
Finish with fresh local herbs. Serve with rice.
tips: Vegetarian version of the classic Bai with added onion and garlic for flavour.
Simple and nutritious.

title: Hmarcha Rawt
jainNotes: Contains garlic (optional). For Jain version, omit garlic and use only chilli, salt, and tomato.
recipe: Crush or pound fresh chillies with salt and garlic (and tomato if desired) into a coarse, fiery chutney.
Serve as the essential spicy accompaniment to any Mizo meal.
tips: The classic Mizo chilli chutney – tangy, spicy and addictive.
Adjust heat to preference.

title: Smoked Pork with Mustard Leaves
jainNotes: Contains pork - not consumed by Jains.
recipe: Cook the pork until tender. Add mustard leaves and continue cooking until the greens wilt and the flavours blend.
Season simply. Serve with rice.
tips: Mustard leaves add a distinctive peppery note to the rich pork.
A classic combination.

title: Sanpiau
jainNotes: Contains fried chicken/fish and onion - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Fried chicken or fish, chilli chutney, crispy rice wafers, onion, coriander

recipe: Prepare a soft rice porridge. Top with layers of crispy fried rice wafers, chilli chutney, fried chicken or fish, onion and coriander.
Eat mixed together – a popular street-food style dish.
tips: Street-food favourite in Aizawl and beyond.
The contrast of soft porridge and crunchy toppings is key.

title: Chhangban
jainNotes: Ingredients are Jain-compatible (sticky rice, optional salt/jaggery). No onion, garlic, or root vegetables.
recipe: Soak and grind sticky rice into a paste or use whole grains. Steam or cook into dense rice cakes or bread-like pieces.
Eat plain, with jaggery, or as a snack with tea.
tips: Traditional sticky-rice snack – portable and filling.
Often carried to the fields.

title: Bekang
jainNotes: Ingredients are Jain-compatible (fermented soybeans, salt/chilli). No onion, garlic, or root vegetables. Verify fermentation process.
recipe: Bekang is traditionally prepared by fermenting cooked soybeans. Once ready, it can be eaten as is or lightly seasoned.
Use as a side, snack, or flavouring agent in Bai and other dishes.
tips: Mizo fermented soybean – similar to Japanese natto in concept.
Pungent and protein-rich.

title: Bamboo Shoot Stir-fry
jainNotes: Contains onion and garlic - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion-garlic.

ingredients.name: Onion, garlic, local herbs, green chilli, salt, a little oil

recipe: Slice bamboo shoot and stir-fry briefly with onion, garlic, chilli, herbs and a touch of oil.
Season with salt. Serve as a crisp side with rice.
tips: Highlights the fresh, crunchy texture of young bamboo shoot.
Minimal seasoning preserves the natural taste.

title: Simple Dal
jainNotes: Contains onion and garlic - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion-garlic.

ingredients.name: Onion, garlic, salt, optional chilli or local herbs

recipe: Boil the lentils with onion, garlic and salt until soft. Keep the consistency light.
Optionally temper with a little chilli or herbs. Serve with rice as a simple side.
tips: Mizos use dal more sparingly than in mainland India; it is a supporting dish.
Kept mild to complement other flavours.
